title: Be Certain of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of being absolutely certain of God, using the story of Elijah and the widow of Zarephath. He emphasizes that after meeting God's requirements, believers must stand firm in faith even when circumstances seem hopeless, trusting that God will keep His Word.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith that stops Jesus despite obstacles. He draws parallels to the present, urging the audience to cry out to Jesus as the provided Lamb for their needs. The sermon includes a prayer line with healings and words of knowledge.

title: Simeon And Anna
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Simeon and Anna, emphasizing the Holy Spirit's guidance and God's faithfulness to His promises. He draws parallels to the present day, encouraging believers to be led by the Spirit and to expect God's miraculous works.

title: Strait Is The Gate
summary: William Branham warns that the gate to eternal life is narrow and few will find it, comparing the current generation to the days of Noah and Sodom. He emphasizes that outward religious acts like speaking in tongues or performing miracles do not guarantee salvation; only a genuine, humble heart transformed by God will enter the Kingdom.

title: What Does Thou Here?
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Elijah, emphasizing the need to hear the 'still small voice' of God amidst the noise of the world. He contrasts the spectacular signs of wind, earthquake, and fire with the quiet voice that truly carries God's presence, urging believers to seek depth and humility rather than outward displays.

title: Living, Dying, Buried, Rising, Coming
subtitle: 59-0329S
summary: William Branham delivers an Easter sermon focusing on five key aspects of Christ's work: His life of love, His sacrificial death, His burial carrying away sins, His resurrection as God's receipt of payment, and His promised return. He emphasizes the hope and assurance believers have through Christ's completed work.

title: Water Baptism
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical basis for water baptism by immersion in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, contrasting it with sprinkling and trinitarian formulas. He dedicates several infants and then baptizes eighteen candidates, emphasizing that baptism must follow the apostolic pattern found in Acts.

title: The Sign Of The Messiah
subtitle: 59-0329E
summary: William Branham preaches on the Messianic sign of knowing the secrets of the heart, demonstrating that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He calls the sick to believe and receive healing through the Holy Spirit's presence and power.

title: Living, Dying, Buried, Rising, Coming
summary: William Branham preaches on the five words: Living, Dying, Buried, Rising, Coming, focusing on Christ's love, death, burial, resurrection, and second coming. He emphasizes the need for divine love in the church and calls for repentance and revival.

title: What Is The Works Of God?
summary: William Branham explores the nature of God's works, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He argues that the same signs that identified Jesus as the Messiah—such as discerning thoughts and revealing secrets—must be present in the Church today through the Holy Spirit. Branham calls for unity among believers and warns against attributing the Spirit's work to the devil, which constitutes the unpardonable sin.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit in the Church
The danger of blaspheming the Holy Spirit
The unity of the Body of Christ

title: It Was Not So From The Beginning
subtitle: 59-0405A
summary: William Branham preaches on returning to the original Pentecostal experience, emphasizing that the church must go back to the beginning where the Holy Spirit had full sway. He argues that modern creeds and denominations have departed from the foundational doctrines of the early church, such as divine healing, speaking in tongues, and water baptism by immersion. Using Matthew 19:8 as a text, he calls believers to abandon man-made traditions and seek the same power and joy experienced at Pentecost.

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: William Branham preaches on the Queen of Sheba's journey to hear Solomon's wisdom, drawing a parallel to the present generation's need to seek the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes that the same Jesus who performed miracles is alive today and calls for unity among believers. The sermon concludes with a prayer line and an appeal for faith in Christ's presence.

title: Led by the Spirit
summary: William Branham preaches on being led by the Holy Spirit, using the biblical account of Simeon and Anna recognizing the infant Jesus in the temple. He shares a personal testimony of being led to pray for a dying boy, emphasizing that God's promises are sure and that the same Spirit leads believers today.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith and the presence of Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever. He connects Bartimaeus's cry for mercy to the need for spiritual and physical healing today, and demonstrates the gift of discernment as a sign of Christ's resurrection power.

title: Mary's Belief
summary: William Branham preaches on Mary's faith in God's promise, using her example to encourage the congregation to take God at His Word for revival and healing. He recounts testimonies of healings, including a baby healed of cancer and a congressman healed from a wheelchair, and calls for a fresh outpouring of the Holy Spirit.

title: Looking At The Unseen
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of looking beyond the physical and temporal to the spiritual and eternal, using examples from the Bible such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, Joshua, Daniel, and the Hebrew children. He emphasizes that faith comes from hearing God's Word and allowing the Holy Spirit to lead, rather than being guided by what the eyes see.

title: Testimony
subtitle: 59-0411B
summary: William Branham shares a testimony of a blind colored girl healed in Jonesboro, Arkansas, fourteen years prior, emphasizing that healings are not mental but physical through faith in Jesus Christ. He recounts his humble beginnings and the power of God honoring simple faith, urging listeners to accept what Jesus has done for them.

title: Watching His Star
location: Angelus Temple, Los Angeles, California, U.S.A.
subtitle: 59-0411E
summary: William Branham preaches on the wise men who followed the star to find Jesus, drawing parallels to the Holy Spirit as the sign leading believers to Christ today. He emphasizes the need for expectancy and faith to recognize God's signs, and demonstrates the Spirit's work through words of knowledge and healings.

title: Be Certain of God
location: Angelus Temple, Los Angeles, California, U.S.A.
subtitle: 59-0412A
summary: William Branham encourages believers to be certain of God's promises, using the story of the widow of Zarephath and Elijah to illustrate that when we meet God's requirements, we can trust Him to fulfill His Word. He shares testimonies of healings and miracles, emphasizing that faith must be acted upon and held onto even when answers are delayed.

title: What Hearest Thou, Elijah?
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Elijah, focusing on his experiences at Mount Carmel, the juniper tree, and the cave. He emphasizes the importance of listening to the still small voice of God rather than being distracted by noisy manifestations, and calls the church to repentance and faith in God's supernatural power.

title: Thirsting for Life
summary: William Branham preaches on the deep spiritual thirst that God places in every human heart, which can only be satisfied by the Holy Spirit. He contrasts worldly attempts to quench this thirst with the true satisfaction found in Christ, using the analogy of a wounded deer panting for water. The sermon includes prayer for the sick, a call to repentance, and an altar invitation.

title: God's Provided Way
summary: William Branham preaches on the parable of the wedding supper from Matthew 22, emphasizing that many are called but few are chosen. He stresses the necessity of receiving the Holy Spirit as the robe of righteousness, warning against entering by any other way than through Jesus Christ. He urges urgency in preparing for Christ's coming, drawing parallels to the days of Noah and Lot.

title: The Faith of Abraham
summary: William Branham teaches on the faith of Abraham as the model for believers, emphasizing that Christians are Abraham's Seed through Christ and must possess Abraham's unwavering faith in God's promises. He contrasts Abraham's patient trust with modern unbelief, urging separation from worldliness and full acceptance of divine healing and all redemptive blessings.

title: JEHOVAH-JIREH
location: Angelus Temple, Echo Park, Los Angeles
summary: William Branham preaches on the faith of Abraham, focusing on God's covenant with Abraham and his seed. He emphasizes that believers are heirs to the same promises, including divine healing and resurrection, and uses the story of Abraham and Sarah's rejuvenation as a type of the believer's transformation at Christ's coming.
themes: the Holy Spirit in the church

title: A Time Of Decision
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of making a decision for God, using the story of Abraham's servant Eliezer finding a wife for Isaac as a type of the Church's relationship with Christ. He urges listeners to trust God's supernatural signs rather than human reasoning, and to commit fully to Christ without delay.

title: My Life Story
summary: William Branham shares his life story, from his birth in a Kentucky mountain cabin to his early encounters with the supernatural. He recounts a vision at age three and a voice at age seven that told him not to drink, smoke, or defile his body, preparing him for a future ministry. He also describes his struggles with poverty, his father's moonshining, and his early disdain for smoking and modern women.

title: Show Us The Father And It Will Satisfy Us
summary: William Branham preaches on the desire to see God, using John 14:7-8 as a text. He explores four ways to see God: in His universe, in His Word, in His Son, and in His people. Through personal anecdotes and biblical examples, he encourages faith and trust in God's presence and promises.

title: Abraham's Seed
summary: William Branham preaches on faith using the example of Abraham, emphasizing that believers are Abraham's seed and heirs to God's promises through Christ. He encourages the congregation to separate from unbelief, trust God's Word unconditionally, and call things that are not as though they were.

title: The Faith of Abraham
summary: William Branham discusses the faith of Abraham, emphasizing God's covenant and the importance of believing God's promises despite physical circumstances. He draws parallels between Abraham's experience and the modern believer's walk of faith, highlighting the need for the Holy Spirit as confirmation of faith.
themes: The Last Sign to the Church

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the Mount of Transfiguration, emphasizing the command 'Hear ye Him' as the ultimate directive to listen to Jesus Christ, who is God's beloved Son. He contrasts the law and prophets with Christ's mercy and love, urging believers to heed Christ alone for salvation, healing, and eternal life.

title: Mother's Day
subtitle: 59-0510M
summary: William Branham speaks on Mother's Day, emphasizing the importance of mothers and the hope of the resurrection. He shares personal testimonies of healings and reflects on the reunion with loved ones in the resurrection, urging listeners to rededicate their lives to God.

title: Who Is This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the triumphal entry of Jesus into Jerusalem, drawing parallels to the present-day expectation of Christ's return. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is forerunning the Second Coming through signs, wonders, and healings, and challenges listeners to recognize Jesus as the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: Images Of Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on what it truly means to be a Christian, emphasizing that it is not about outward symbols or church membership but about being inwardly transformed into the image of Christ through the Holy Spirit. He uses the example of Jesus washing the disciples' feet to illustrate the servant nature of true Christianity, calling believers to humility and love for one another.

title: As I Thought On My Ways
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of reflecting on one's ways and turning to God's testimonies, especially in times of trouble. He uses personal anecdotes and biblical examples to illustrate how trouble often drives people to seek God, and urges the congregation to turn to God now rather than waiting for crisis.

title: The Time Of Decision
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of making a decisive choice for God, using the biblical account of Rebekah's decision to go with Abraham's servant to marry Isaac. He emphasizes the urgency of responding to the Holy Spirit's call and the importance of trusting in the old-time Pentecostal experience.

title: All The Days Of Our Life
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for complete surrender to God, contrasting man's desire for his own way with God's plan. He emphasizes that true Christian life is a continual sacrifice and that believers are bondslaves of Christ, serving Him in holiness all the days of their life.

title: Thirsting for Life
summary: William Branham speaks on the soul's thirst for God, contrasting worldly pleasures with eternal life. He shares a testimony from India where a blind man was healed, and urges believers to live as sons and daughters of the King.

title: Balm in Gilead
summary: William Branham preaches on Jeremiah 8:22, asking why God's people are not healed when there is balm in Gilead. He argues that people refuse God's remedy for sin and unbelief, and calls for repentance and receiving the Holy Spirit.

title: A Deceived Church, By The World
summary: William Branham uses the story of Samson and Delilah to illustrate how the church has been deceived by the world, losing its spiritual power through compromise, organization, and worldly wisdom. He calls for a return to the Holy Ghost and the new birth, warning that the church's strength has been shaved off by worldliness.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation on topics including spiritual gifts, salvation and the Holy Ghost, Communion, and the fall of Satan. He emphasizes the importance of the Holy Spirit in interpreting Scripture and warns against mixing with unbelievers.

title: Thinking On Our Ways
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of self-examination and repentance, using the text 'I thought on my ways, and turned my feet unto thy testimonies' (Psalm 119:59). He shares personal stories and biblical examples to illustrate that troubles often drive people to God, but urges believers to think on their ways and turn to God before trouble strikes. The sermon emphasizes confession of sins, living righteously, and having a clear conscience before God.
themes: God as a present help in trouble
The importance of a clear conscience
The blood of Jesus for cleansing

title: Balm in Gilead
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme that God has provided a remedy for sin and sickness through Jesus Christ, but people refuse to receive it due to unbelief. He emphasizes the need for the new birth and the baptism of the Holy Spirit, and calls listeners to repent and accept God's provision.

title: Dedication Of Building, To The Lord
summary: William Branham dedicates a church building, using the Old Testament tabernacle as a type to explain the three-room house of God: justification, sanctification, and baptism of the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes the necessity of the Blood of Christ for fellowship and warns against denominational barriers, calling for unity among all believers.

title: A Total Deliverance
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for complete surrender to God and unity within the church, using the Exodus account of Moses and the deliverance of Israel as a type. He emphasizes that total deliverance from sin and sickness comes when everything is brought under the Blood of Christ, and the church is unified in heart and accord.

title: Without Money Or Without Price
summary: William Branham preaches on Isaiah 55, emphasizing that salvation and spiritual blessings are free gifts from God, not to be bought with money. He contrasts worldly pursuits that cost money but bring no lasting satisfaction with the free offer of eternal life through Christ. Using examples like the healing at the Beautiful Gate and the prodigal son, he calls listeners to come to God without price.

title: The Reaction To An Action
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of drawing nigh to God and confessing sins before prayer, using the story of the widow of Zarephath to illustrate how faith mixed with God's Word and Spirit can bring provision and healing. He encourages believers to hold fast to their testimony and trust God even in dark times.

title: Discerning The Body Of The Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of discerning the Body of the Lord, which is the Church, and warns against taking communion unworthily. He calls for spiritual discernment in all aspects of Christian life, including healing, the baptism of the Holy Spirit, and recognizing the signs of the times. Branham emphasizes that the same signs given to Sodom will be given to this generation before Christ's return.

title: Why?
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of 'Why?'—why there is sin and sickness in the world despite God's provision of healing and the Holy Spirit. He uses the metaphor of a balm in Gilead to illustrate that God has provided a cure for sin and sickness, but people refuse to take it due to stubbornness and pride. He calls for repentance and receiving the Holy Spirit.

title: As I Thought On My Ways
summary: William Branham reflects on the importance of turning to God in times of trouble, using personal stories and biblical examples to illustrate that God is a present help. He urges listeners to examine their lives, repent, and commit to following Christ before it is too late.

title: Planting The Vine And Where To Plant It
summary: William Branham preaches on Psalm 80, using the metaphor of a vine to describe God's people. He contrasts the true vine, Christ, with wild vines of denominationalism and unbelief, urging believers to be planted by the rivers of water—the Holy Spirit—to bear spiritual fruit.

title: What Went Ye Out To See?
summary: William Branham preaches on the question Jesus asked about John the Baptist: 'What went ye out to see?' He contrasts the world, the lukewarm church, and true believers, emphasizing that God uses simple, anointed people to accomplish His purposes. Branham calls believers to dedicate their hands and lives to Christ, doing whatever is in their power for the Gospel.

title: Who Is This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the triumphal entry of Jesus into Jerusalem, using the crowd's question 'Who is this?' to draw parallels to the present-day work of the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit's manifestations—healing, discernment, and transformation—cause the world to question, just as they did when Jesus rode into Jerusalem. Branham calls believers to make a decision for Christ and prepare for His second coming.

title: Why Cry? Speak!
summary: William Branham preaches on Exodus 14:15-16, urging believers to stop crying to God and instead speak His Word and go forward. He emphasizes that God's anointed messengers must be obeyed, and that the same Holy Spirit who worked in Jesus works today through signs and wonders. The sermon calls for faith and action rather than doubt and complaint.

title: Possessing The Enemy's Gates
summary: William Branham preaches on the promise that Abraham's seed will possess the gates of their enemies, drawing from Genesis 24 and 22. He emphasizes that believers, as spiritual seed of Abraham, are heirs to this promise and must endure testing before receiving it. The sermon encourages faith in God's promises over natural circumstances, citing biblical examples of those who possessed enemy gates through faith.

title: My New Ministry
summary: William Branham shares a personal experience in the woods where God confirms a new phase of his ministry through the power of spoken words, demonstrating that whatever one says in faith can come to pass. He recounts how the Holy Spirit instructed him to speak and materialize his desires, using the example of calling squirrels to him. This marks a transition from his previous ministry of visions to a greater authority in spoken faith.

title: Thy Seed Shall Possess The Gate Of His Enemy
location: Santa Clara County Fairgrounds, San Jose, California, U.S.A.
summary: William Branham preaches on the promise that Abraham's seed shall possess the gate of their enemies, drawing from Genesis 24 and 22. He connects this promise to believers in Christ, who as Abraham's seed through faith, have victory over every enemy including sickness, sin, and death. The sermon culminates in a call for repentance and healing, with demonstrations of the Holy Spirit's discernment and power.

title: Speak to This Mountain
summary: William Branham discusses the Scripture Mark 11:23 about speaking to a mountain and having faith. He shares personal experiences of the Holy Spirit's leading, including a vision about a fish coming back to life and a warning about a trap set for him. He emphasizes the importance of being careful with words and the new ministry beginning.
themes: the new ministry of speaking to mountains

title: Balm in Gilead
summary: William Branham preaches on the spiritual condition of the church and the world, using Jeremiah 8:22 to ask why God's people remain sick when there is balm in Gilead. He emphasizes the need for genuine new birth and the inoculation of the Holy Spirit to overcome sin and unbelief.

title: From The Beginning It Wasn't So
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of God's Word, contrasting it with man-made traditions and creeds. He emphasizes that the Church must return to the Pentecostal experience of the early believers, where signs and wonders followed. Using Matthew 19:8 as a text, he argues that many modern teachings deviate from what was true 'from the beginning.'

title: Jehovah of Miracles
summary: William Branham preaches on the Annunciation to Mary, emphasizing the importance of taking God at His Word without doubting. He contrasts Mary's faith with Zacharias's doubt and encourages believers to believe God's promises despite impossibilities. The sermon also touches on the power of the name of Jesus and the need for unity and sincerity in the church.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing that faith in Jesus Christ can bring healing and salvation. He contrasts Bartimaeus's persistent faith with the unbelief of the religious leaders, and encourages the congregation to trust in the Lamb of God who is present to heal and save today.

title: Door To The Heart
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:20, emphasizing that Jesus stands at the door of the human heart and knocks, but the latch is on the inside—only the individual can open. He explores various 'doors' within the heart, such as pride, private life, faith, and spiritual sight, urging listeners to let Jesus be not only Savior but also Lord, allowing Him full access to transform their lives.

title: Let Us See God
summary: William Branham preaches on seeing God in four ways: in His universe, in His Word, in His Son, and in His people. He shares personal stories from nature and his ministry to illustrate God's presence and power.

title: What Is The Holy Ghost?
summary: William Branham teaches on the nature and purpose of the Holy Ghost, describing it as a sign, seal, and the Spirit of Christ in believers. He emphasizes that the Holy Ghost is a covenant promise to Abraham's seed, which includes all who are in Christ, and that it seals believers until the day of redemption.

title: Questions and Answers on the Holy Ghost
summary: William Branham addresses questions about the Holy Ghost, clarifying the biblical account of Pentecost and the distinction between speaking in tongues as a gift versus the initial evidence of receiving the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes that the Holy Spirit is received by faith according to God's laws, and that true baptism of the Holy Ghost is evidenced by a transformed life and the manifestation of God's presence, not necessarily by speaking in unknown tongues.
themes: Initial evidence of the Holy Spirit

title: Identified With Christ
summary: William Branham discusses the human desire to identify with an example, and how people often choose worldly figures like movie stars or cowboys instead of Jesus Christ. He explains that true identification with Christ comes through repentance and baptism, which unites believers with His death, burial, and resurrection. Branham also addresses questions about speaking in tongues and the Holy Spirit, emphasizing that the fruit of the Spirit, especially love, is the true evidence of receiving the Holy Ghost.

title: Questions and Answers
summary: William Branham answers questions from the congregation on topics including demonology, the fate of the spirits that entered the swine, the nature of eternal life, the importance of the Holy Ghost, and predestination. He emphasizes that only God has eternal life and that believers receive it through the Holy Spirit, becoming part of God and unable to perish. He also warns against religious deception and the need to earnestly seek the Holy Ghost.

title: A Super Sign
summary: William Branham delivers a Christmas message centered on Isaiah 7:10-16, presenting the virgin birth of Immanuel as God's eternal super sign. He contrasts human achievements like the Titanic and Hitler's fortifications with God's humble sign of a baby, emphasizing that God dwells with His people. Branham connects this sign to the present evening light revival, where the same works of God are manifested through believers.

title: A Super Sense
summary: William Branham speaks on the concept of a 'super sense'—faith—which is the sixth sense given to Christians that governs and surpasses the five natural senses. He emphasizes that this super sense enables believers to believe God's Word contrary to physical evidence, and he illustrates this with testimonies of healings.

title: And From That Time
summary: In this New Year's Eve sermon, William Branham emphasizes the necessity of a personal encounter with God that brings eternal change, contrasting it with temporary New Year's resolutions. He illustrates through biblical figures like Abraham, Moses, Mary, Peter, and Paul how meeting God transforms a person forever. Branham urges listeners to seek a genuine meeting with God rather than merely turning a new page.
